description: Nitrogen is a chemical element with symbol N and atomic number 7. It is a nonmetal and the lightest member of group 15 of the periodic table. At standard temperature and pressure, two atoms bond to form N2, a colorless and odorless diatomic gas that comprises about 78% of Earth's atmosphere.
uses: Elemental nitrogen is used as an inert gas for commercial uses such as food packaging and as liquid nitrogen in cryogenic applications. Many industrially important compounds containing nitrogen, such as ammonia, nitric acid, and organic nitrates, are used as propellants and explosives. Synthetically produced ammonia and nitrates serve as key industrial fertilizers, while nitrogen is also a constituent of organic compounds used in high-strength fabrics and superglue. Nitrogen is a constituent of every major pharmacological drug class, including antibiotics.
characteristics: Nitrogen has one of the highest electronegativities among elements at 3.04 on the Pauling scale. The element features an extremely strong triple bond in its elemental form (N≡N), which is the second strongest bond in any diatomic molecule after carbon monoxide. Nitrogen has a melting point of −210 °C and a boiling point of −196 °C, much lower than the rest of its group due to weak van der Waals interactions between N2 molecules.
